newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Britain's Blair seeks freer EU, Commonwealth trade.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair seeks freer EU, Commonwealth trade.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair said on Monday his Labour Party would champion freer trade between European and Commonwealth countries if it became his country's next government.
Addressing the Commonwealth Press Union in Cape Town and at a news conference later, Blair repeatedly attacked the protectionist tendencies of the European Union.
He said the Commonwealth, which links Britain and its former colonies, should hammer out a new commitment to free trade at its heads of government meeting in Edinburgh in October next year.

"If we are elected, a new Labour government will use that meeting to propose an economic declaration...with concrete proposals to increase trade and economic cooperation between member states and expand opportunities for direct investment," he said.
He said the declaration could be an addendum to the 1991 Harare Declaration committing Commonwealth countries to democracy, human rights and good governance.

In what British observers said appeared to be a keynote address laying down central themes for the Labour Party's campaign for the next general election in Britain, Blair promised to help Africa fight the "Fortress Europe" tendency in the EU.
He pledged Labour Party support for reform of the EU's common agricultural policy and freer access to European markets for countries outside the region.
Responding to questions, he said the party would help South Africa to fight for a fair deal in its negotiations with the EU on a free trade area agreement.
The EU has denied South Africa full access to the Lome Convention on preferential trade terms for Africa, the Caribbean and Pacific, saying the country's economy is too strong.
Under pressure mainly from France, EU negotiators have been given a restrictive mandate to negotiate with President Nelson Mandela's new democracy on free access to European markets.
The mandate excludes a host of agricultural sectors regarded as sensitive in Europe, but mainly representing South Africa's own strengths.
"If the European Union becomes an enclosed free trade area within itself that is effectively preventing free trade elsewhere in the world, it would be a retrogressive step," Blair said.

"If you end up with a better developed Africa and developing world then those are markets for our goods as well. There are people there with more money to spend...there is a commonality of interests there that we should be developing."
He said he also would support the expansion of the European Union, adding: "It is important that the emerging Euroepan democracies participate in the EU."
